summary.text: A man aged 44 was admitted on 15 December 2015 with dull abdominal pain, bloating under the left rib cage and a big painless palpable mass on the left side of the abdomen. He was afebrile with normal vitals, without nausea or vomiting.

Laboratory tests were normal except mild leucocytosis, with unremarkable tumor markers and moderately elevated C-reactive protein and fibrinogen. Ultrasonography and CT showed a unilocular 12 cm splenic cyst characterized as simple; anti-Echinococcus serology was negative and chest X-ray unremarkable. Laparoscopic cyst fenestration with omentoplasty was chosen and he was evaluated by a pulmonologist and cardiologist.

At laparoscopy the cyst had a thickened wall with adherent omentum and did not correspond to a simple cyst; daughter cysts found after opening showed it was a hydatid cyst. Surgery stayed laparoscopic with saline gauze packing, aspiration, germinative membrane removal, partial pericystectomy and omentoplasty. Histology of the membrane and content was consistent with hydatid disease, without scolices.

Recovery was very good with discharge on the third postoperative day. Albendazole was prescribed in two 4-week cycles separated by 2 weeks to prevent recurrence. He was followed every six months for four years by abdominal ultrasound and CT, with no evidence of recurrence.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the six JPEGs are inspected in the separate visual submission.
Medical history is described only as not remarkable; no individual history items are recorded.
Discussion paragraphs describe the literature and the authors' opinions, not the patient, and are not patient facts.
No absolute times are given for the surgery or the albendazole course; only the admission date is stated.

Timeline left partial on purpose: the baseline laboratory evaluation and the albendazole prescription have no literal order against other events (no on-admission wording for the labs; "to prevent recurrence" names a goal, not an order), so they are not linked.
The planned laparoscopic cyst fenestration was superseded intraoperatively by partial pericystectomy; the source never states it was cancelled, so it stays a planned procedure.
